flagged.urlStatus: Loaded (docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/dr-scenarios-for-data). It supports the backup half: backups restore a known good state after corruption. It does not say that replication copies corruption to the replicas, so the first sentence of the explanation has no support on this page. Cloud SQL's replication page (opened) even says a replica can be promoted 'to replace an instance that's corrupted'.
flagged.evidence: dr-scenarios-for-data: "Backups are made as part of a recovery plan either to recover from a corruption of data so that you can restore to a known good state..." Spanner backups overview: "You can restore the backups when operator or application errors cause logical data corruption." https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/backup . Cloud SQL: "You can also promote a replica to replace an instance that's corrupted." https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/replication
flagged.problem: The answer 'false' is right because a live replica holds no earlier point in time to restore. But the cited page never says replication spreads corruption. 'Corrupted data' is also loose wording: Cloud SQL documents promoting a replica when an instance is corrupted, so an expert could object. The card holds only for logical corruption (operator or application errors).
flagged.suggestedFix: Statement: "When an application error corrupts records, a live replica lets a business restore the data as it was before the error, just as a historical backup does." (false). Explanation: "A live replica copies changes as they happen, so records corrupted by an application or operator error are copied too. A backup keeps an earlier known good state that can be restored." Sources: https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/dr-scenarios-for-data plus https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/backup ("restore the backups when operator or application errors cause logical data corruption").
